title: Source-free proof review of the frozen canonical-pair bitstream writer
timing: Root reports the prospectively clarified protocol was fixed before implementation and new counts. Producer read only the live route, the two contract files and old predecessor prose/code definitions; no GDT1300empirical file or model was opened. This records a mathematical review, not independent experimental validation.
verdict: No source-free mathematical flaw found in the clarified fixed contract. Empirical feasibility, implementation correctness, lookup-entry cap and all statistical decisions remain unassessed.

canonical_token_lemma.premises: Finite token vocabulary containing all singleton working units and selected pairs M; every pair token belongs to M. Greedy parsing consumes a matching pair at the current cursor, else one singleton, and restarts at each visible word boundary.
canonical_token_lemma.necessary_and_sufficient_condition: After a singleton x with a following token beginning y, xy must not be in M. No additional restriction follows a pair token.
canonical_token_lemma.necessity: If a singleton x is followed by a token beginning y and xy is selected, greedy parsing consumes xy across the intended boundary; the intended token list is not recovered.
canonical_token_lemma.sufficiency: Induct at each intended boundary. A next pair is in M and is consumed exactly. A next singleton either ends the word or has no selected pair crossing to the following first unit, so is consumed alone. The induction recovers every intended token and hence T.
canonical_token_lemma.scope: Self-pairs and mutually overlapping candidate pairs are allowed. A consumed pair's second unit is not reconsidered as a new cursor. This extends1253's prior one-pair principle; it is not proof of native linguistic units.

nonempty_choices_and_termination.allowed_singletons: For a fixed preceding singleton x, at most16different y can have xy in M. Of22singleton token choices, at least6therefore remain. After a pair all38tokens remain available. Positive2count+1weights give complete finite binary Huffman trees with more than one leaf.
nonempty_choices_and_termination.count_tree: T ranges over1..13with positive weights. No zero-token word exists; the count tree is also nondegenerate. TRAIN overflow is a stop, not truncation or support extension.
nonempty_choices_and_termination.message_tree: The declared source alphabet contains ordinary source characters and a distinct END. Require a nonempty END code; the actual declared multi-character source alphabet yields a nondegenerate finite tree. Empty ordinary content is encoded as END.
nonempty_choices_and_termination.finite_progress: Each output word consumes at least one count-code bit and one token-code bit. Its token count is finite. Finite source bits therefore start only finitely many words, and virtual zero completion finishes the last one after finitely many tree traversals.
nonempty_choices_and_termination.word_width: At most13tokens of length at most2give at most26working units, below the frozen48-unit line width. No token or word must be silently split to wrap.

inverse_proof: The canonical token lemma makes each generated written word recover its original tokens and T.

Those tokens and T determine the same role sequence, previous-token class, exact singleton filter and Huffman table at every step. Their public codewords recover exactly the binary choices consumed by the writer.
Concatenating recovered codes across words produces the original source bitstream followed by a possibly empty string of zero padding. Word spaces and line breaks do not alter that bitstream.

The source Huffman code is prefix-free and END is not ordinary input. Decoding until the first END therefore recovers exactly the complete input string, including original projected spaces and newlines.
If two different source strings had the same output, deterministic decoding would recover both, a contradiction. The writer is injective on its declared source domain.

Conversely, accepted ciphertexts must have a source END, an all-zero recovered tail and identical canonical reencoding. Reencoding is needed to reject overlong zero completion and extra zero-driven words; a zero-tail check alone is not sufficient.
boundary_and_cost_checks: If real bits end during count decoding, finish that count with zeros and then produce all of that word's tokens. If they end at a completed word boundary, stop without another word.

The precise output Huffman mapping after a bare unit depends on its exact identity when M filters successors, even though weights use its binary class. The frozen cap correctly counts the actual filtered mappings, not just base weight rows.
The1200-entry cap is an empirical construction-cost gate, not a theorem guaranteed by16pairs. Its failure must stop before source generation.

The exact sign order was missing from the initial text and was fixed prospectively by root in SPEC and the protocol. TRAIN T>13was likewise explicitly resolved to stop before encoding. This review binds those clarified bytes.
Canonical output-unit parsing assumes the declared22working units and explicit output-word spaces. It supplies no new physical alphabet or word-boundary evidence.
Messages are individually delimited ciphertext objects. Internal source paragraph newlines are ordinary source characters; no hidden output-layout reset is introduced.
Outside-alphabet source characters, literal input END, malformed codewords, missing END, nonzero post-END bits and extra noncanonical words are errors, not fallback spellings.
hand_reasoned_fixtures_no_execution: M={ab,bc}: tokens[ab,c] and[ab,bc]are canonical;[a,bc]is not. This catches checking only the next singleton rather than the first unit of any next token.
M containing aa: [aa,a]is the greedy parse of aaa. Pair tokens need no constraint against the first unit of their successor; [a,a]is noncanonical.
A final bare x is legal even if some selected pair starts x, since there is no next unit within that word. Never test a pair across visible word spaces.
Source END ending inside a T code must finish a whole positive-T word; END ending exactly at a word boundary must not create a further word.
Appending an extra word produced wholly from zero bits can satisfy the zero-tail test but must fail canonical reencoding.

Empty source, a source with spaces/newlines, and a changed source must retain respectively empty content, exact separators and the changed message under the same fixed key. These are proposed fixtures, not reported test results.
scientific_limits: Huffman probabilities under fair bits are2^(-length), not the smoothed frequency fractions. Character-Huffman encoding does not prove natural source bits are IID or fair.
A good ideal output model does not imply that the actual source-driven writer has the same statistics. The pinned protocol correctly separates these controls.
Legal greedy coverage is largely guaranteed and cannot select a native key or meaning.1253's universal-cover caution remains.
Old1181/1182/1193/1195failures and1223/1225comparison-scope limits are not rescued. A joint pass would be a synthetic control only.
administrative_scope: One separate producer proof note plus one RAW proposal/ideas-add. No code, toy execution, native count, target image, semantic assignment or root-file edit.
